measures.action: Shut off the fans and ventilation so the air stops moving.

effect.text: Engineering proposal (hypothesis for the engine): with less airflow the flame spreads slower or starves (ACME BRE, PSI-20: flames went out in still air at 21 % O2 in microgravity). In this model the effect depends on oxygen and gravity; it is not tested for this place.
effect.src: Hypothesis for the engine; effect basis PSI-20 ACME BRE, DOI 10.60555/vb93-3y72 (flames in still air at 21 % O2 in microgravity). No lunar-gravity combustion data exists (LUCI and FM2 are the first)

measures.action: Use a portable extinguisher on the burning part before the fire grows.

effect.text: Engineering proposal (hypothesis): the engine puts out the fire where it started at that moment. No extinguisher of the lunar module is documented in the sources used here.
effect.src: Hypothesis; no test in the sources used

measures.action: Put a fire-blocking barrier between the ascent stage and the descent stage so a fire cannot cross.

effect.text: Engineering proposal (hypothesis): the engine removes this connection. A barrier breaks the continuous fuel path that the model assumes. No test of such a barrier exists in the sources used.
effect.src: Hypothesis; flame spread needs continuous fuel (stated, not measured, for this place)

gaps: The lunar module is labelled by mesh-name prefix (the 134 meshes have opaque names): 6 components were identified from highlight views of the model, with medium to low confidence; the rest are listed as unidentified.
Gravity at 0.166 g is an extrapolation: PSI holds no partial-gravity combustion data (LUCI 2025 and FM2 are the first).
No PSI/NTRS combustion test exists for the lunar module or its materials; spread speeds are the SAFFIRE anchor scaled by estimated factors.

Energetic components: none verified. The lunar module carried oxygen, propellant and helium tanks, but none was verified with a source here and none is a separately labelled part of the model, so there is no rupture.
The landing gear and the antennas are treated as non-combustible metal (assumption): a fire does not spread into them in the model.
The ascent and descent stage labels (polySurfa*, group13_p*) come from the model's shapes by eye; no drawing of the lunar module was used. Detection and crew actions are not modelled.
